Circular summary statistics for trajectories

Source: R/circular_statistics.R
circ_summary.Rd

Computes per-trial or global circular statistics (mean direction, resultant length, concentration) from the step-angle column of a `Tracks`.

Usage

circ_summary(x, w = NULL, by = c("id", "global"), axial = FALSE)

# S4 method for class 'Tracks'
circ_summary(x, w = NULL, by = c("id", "global"), axial = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A [`Tracks`] object.

w

Character. Name of a weight column in `x@data`, used in place of the weight column of `x`. Its values must be finite and `>= 0`; a zero weight excludes an observation. When `NULL` (default), the weight column of `x` is used, and all steps are weighted equally when `x` has none. A group whose weights are all zero is an error (class `radiatR_nonestimable`).

by

Character. `"id"` (default) returns one row per trial; `"global"` pools all observations into a single summary row.

axial

Logical. Treat the angles as axial (bidirectional, mod-pi) data: statistics are computed via the angle-doubling method and the mean is reported as an axis in `[0, pi)` radians / `[0, 180)` degrees. Default `FALSE` (ordinary directional data).

Value

A `data.frame` with columns `id`, `n`, `t_start`, `t_end`, `mean_dir` (radians, unit-circle convention, 0 to 2pi; weighted when weights are used), `resultant_R` (0–1), and `kappa` (von Mises concentration: the maximum-likelihood estimate from the mean resultant length, weighted when weights are used; `NA` for fewer than three valid angles of positive weight, `Inf` when all angles coincide). `n` counts the valid angles whatever their weight. No small-sample bias correction is applied, so kappa is biased upward for small n: circular::mle.vonmises(bias = TRUE) gives a corrected estimate and boot_kappa_ci() reports the bias.

Examples

data(cpunctatus)
head(circ_summary(cpunctatus, by = "id"))
#>        id   n t_start t_end  mean_dir resultant_R      kappa
#> 1 10_10_1 299       1   299 2.2781642   0.1548308  0.3134475
#> 2 10_11_1  65      14    78 0.2543320   0.6671992  1.8194711
#> 3 10_12_1  48       2    49 2.3069985   0.9037793  5.4856988
#> 4 10_13_1  80      22   101 0.9651068   0.5374843  1.2768013
#> 5 10_14_1  30       1    30 4.7633599   0.9718670 18.0335307
#> 6 10_15_1  54       2    55 3.5207738   0.9370359  8.2159697
circ_summary(cpunctatus, by = "global")
#>       id     n t_start t_end   mean_dir resultant_R     kappa
#> 1 global 44331       1   299 0.01906991   0.1247348 0.2514355
